Kevin Menke.b:
Kevin Menke enters his third season as an assistant coach.
In year two, the men finished second in the MVC, and the women took fourth overall in the MAC. Menke also helped Elijah Rolfsen (first male NCAA qualifier in more than 20 years) and Chrisna Bezuidenhout reach the NCAA Championships.
In his first season with the Red and White, he helped lead the men to their fifth straight championship title, which was the first season the RedHawks competed in the Missouri Valley Conference (MVC). The women also secured a third-place finish in the Mid-American Conference (MAC) Women's Swimming & Diving Championships. Senior swimmer Madeline Padavic also secured a spot as an NCAA qualifier and competed at the NCAA Championships.
Menke has more than a decade of coaching experience as a head age group swim coach with the South YMCA Swim Team, a program he initially joined as an assistant in 2013. Menke also served as head swim coach for Crestwood Swim Club from 2014-2018.
He is a former Wright State swimmer and graduated with a Bachelor’s degree in Business Management from WSU in 2016.

Samantha Pitter enters her third season as head coach of the Miami University swimming and diving team.
In her first two seasons as head coach, under her leadership, Miami swimmers have broken a combined 20 program records while continuing to excel academically, with the women's team earning the highest team GPA among all Miami athletic programs in both the Spring 2025 and Spring 2026 semesters. The women’s team has also led the MAC in Academic All-MAC honorees in both seasons under Pitter. In total, Pitter's student-athletes have received 16 CSC Academic All-District honors, 16 Individual Scholar All-America honors and 54 Academic All-MAC honors. The program has also been recognized twice as a CSCAA Fall Scholar All-America Team and two other times as a CSCAA Spring Scholar All-America Team.
In her inaugural season, she led the program to an MVC Championship. This past season, she coached the first male NCAA qualifier in more than 20 years.
NCAA Qualifiers
• Madeline Padavic (2025)
• Chrisna Bezuidenhout (2026)
• Elijah Rolfsen (2026)
Pitter saw significant success in her first year with the RedHawks, as she guided the men to their fifth straight championship title in the teams first season in the Missouri Valley Conference (MVC). Pitter was also named the MVC Men's Swimming Coach of the Year. She led the women to a third-place finish in the Mid-American Conference (MAC) Women's Swimming & Diving Championships.
Pitter arrived to Oxford after serving two years as an associate head coach at the University of Pittsburgh. She brings 16 years of collegiate coaching experience with her to Miami.
From 2022-24, Pitter helped lead the Panthers to break 39 program records, with 25 student-athletes qualifying for the NCAA Championships. In 2023, she assisted the men's program to its most NCAA qualifiers at any point in the school's history. In 2023 and 2024, the men achieved their highest-ever finish in the ACC (seventh each year). From 2023 to 2024, the women's program improved their score by 100 points at the ACC Championships. Most recently, she helped lead the Pitt men to their second-highest NCAA finish ever. She also helped improve the team's GPA to its highest mark in nine years.
Prior to Pittsburgh, Pitter spent eight seasons at Harvard on the coaching staff, including four years as the Associate Head Coach for the men's swimming program. Pitter helped lead Harvard to two consecutive top-15 finishes at the NCAA Championships and five consecutive Ivy League Championships. She also secured three top-25 finishes at the NCAA Championships and won an Ivy League Championship in her first year. During her tenure, the Crimson set over 60 school records. Harvard had four recruiting classes that finished in the top 25 nationally. In total, Pitter's efforts led to 24 NCAA qualifiers, eight NCAA All-Americans, two top-eight relays, seven top-16 relays and two NCAA event titles. On the academic side, Harvard maintained a team GPA in the top two of all Division I swimming & diving teams each semester she coached.
Pitter was the lead coach of Dean Farris, one of Harvard's most accomplished swimmers in the school's history. Under Pitter's guidance, Farris finished his career as a two-time NCAA champion and American record holder while earning 23 All-American accolades.
Prior to Harvard, Pitter spent five years at Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), including four years as an assistant and one year as acting head coach in 2012-13. During her time with the Engineers, she aided each program to three consecutive NEWMAC Championships. Pitter also helped the MIT men to four straight top-10 finishes at the NCAA Division III Championships. She coached MIT's first-ever Olympic Trials qualifier to a 21st-place finish in the 50 freestyle in 2012. In the 2012-13 season, she guided the Engineers to their best NCAA finishes: third place for the men and eighth place for the women. In that same season, the women broke 12 school records, and the men rewrote 21 of 24 school records, which included three NCAA event titles and one NCAA record. Pitter was named NEWMAC Women's Coach of the Year for her team's performance at the NEWMAC Championships.
She also has experience coaching at the national level as a three-time USA National Team coach. Pitter served as an Assistant Olympic Coach for Cape Verde at the Paris Games in 2024.
Pitter earned a double-major Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Communication at Hamilton College in 2007. There, she was a four-time All-America sprinter, school record holder, team captain and NESCAC All-Academic recipient. She later earned a Masters of Education in Physical Education Specializing in Coaching from Boston University in 2011.

Adam Lenz.b:
Lenz begins his second season with the Red and White.
In his first season with the RedHawks, the men finished second in the MVC, and the women took fourth overall in the MAC.
Lenz most recently spent time as an Assistant Coach and Assistant Aquatics Director at Oberlin College and Conservatory Swimming and Diving. In these roles, he drafted team workouts, assisted with recruiting, worked with social media and helped set up the facility and prepare for competition.
Prior to that, he worked with the University of South Dakota Swimming & Diving as a graduate assistant coach from 2022 to 2024. At USD, Lenz created training programs for athletes, helped with recruiting, assisted with logistics and scouting and also operated social media pages.
He worked in the John Carroll University Sports Information Department from 2021 to 2022, assisting with both office work (website management, article writing, photo organization, graphic design) and event work (broadcast crew, photography, social media and statistics).
Lenz also spent time with Chagrin Valley Country Club in 2021 as an Assistant Swim Coach. In this role, he worked on technique with athletes across all skill and developmental levels and served as the Head Lifeguard for the 2021 season. Additionally, he has experience as a camp swim coach/counselor at Stanford swim camps (2022 and 2025) and as a volunteer coach with Cleveland Elite Aquatics (Fall 2019).
Lenz swam for John Carroll University during his time in college. His accomplishments include being a six-time NCAA Division III All-American, two-time NCAA Division III Honorable Mention All-American, two-time CSCAA Division III Scholar All-American, four-time OAC Team Champion and 13 time OAC Champion.
Lenz graduated from John Carroll University in 2022 with a Bachelor of Science in Exercise Science. He most recently earned a Masters degree in Sport Management from the University of South Dakota (2024).

Charlie Retter.b:
Charlie Retter enters his third season as the diving coach for the RedHawks.
In his first two seasons with Miami, eight RedHawks have competed at the NCAA Zone C Championships. He has also had three student-athletes that were named a MAC Diver of the Week.
Retter comes to Oxford after spending the past two years at The Woodlands Diving Academy in Shenandoah, Texas. He previously worked for six years at Duke Diving Club in Durham, N.C. Retter has helped divers qualify for the USA Diving Junior National Championship every year since 2017 and represented USA Diving as part of the coaching staff at the 2023 Junior Pan American Games.
Retter earned his Bachelor’s degree in Sociology from North Carolina State University in 2022 and previously competed for the Wolfpack’s swim/dive team. He also has experience diving internationally as a member of the Junior National Team under Olympic coaches Jenny and Drew Johansen.
